title: Tenant bandwidth-aware scaling controller with headroom guarantees
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem statement:
Customers on Dedicated pools occasionally see latency spikes or degraded throughput when tenant traffic surges collide with global batching decisions. Current autoscaler targets CPU and token throughput at the pool level and lacks visibility into per-tenant bandwidth (requests/sec + token distribution), which makes SLAs brittle for high-priority tenants.

Goal:
Implement a tenant-aware scaling controller that consumes per-tenant throughput metrics and issues capacity changes that preserve per-tenant headroom guarantees. The controller must coordinate with the existing pool autoscaler, enforce safety limits (max step, cooldown, budget caps), and support tiered guarantees (gold/silver/bronze).

Why this work matters:
- Ensures high-priority customers retain effective throughput during noisy-neighbor events.
- Reduces emergency manual interventions and pod-eviction incidents.
- Enables predictable billing and SLA enforcement for Dedicated customers.

Scope / deliverables:
- New controller module: bandwidth-aware target synthesizer that outputs per-tenant desired capacity and a recommended pool-level delta.
- Safety layer: step size limiter, negative scaling soft-floor, cooldown window, and rollback heuristic based on latency regressions.
- Integration with routing: tag per-request tenant and priority so controller uses correct traffic splits.
- Simulation harness and staged canary rollout for 2 Dedicated regions.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting global autoscaler; this is an overlay controller that proposes deltas evaluated by the existing orchestrator.

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Tenant+Bandwidth+Aware+Scaling (internal)
- Perf simulation results: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/scale-sim-tenant (read-only)
acceptance_criteria: Controller produces per-tenant desired capacity every 30s with <500ms compute overhead
Safety limits prevent >40% upscale or >25% downscale in a single step at pool level
Gold-tier tenants maintain 95th percentile latency within 1.2x of baseline during 3x request spikes in sim
Automated rollback triggers on end-to-end tail latency regression >20% after a scale event
E2E canary executed in staging and one US Dedicated region with metrics collected in Grafana
tasks: Spec: formalize metric composition (per-tenant RPS, per-tenant token/sec, queue saturation) and threshold mapping
Impl: synthesizer service that ingests tenant-timeseries and outputs proposed deltas
Impl: safety module with step limiter, cool-down, and negative floor
Integrate: hook controller output into orchestrator accept/reject API
Simulate: run 1000 synthetic tenant spike scenarios and capture regressions
Canary: deploy to staging and us-east-1 dedicated pool, monitor for 48h
Docs: update operator runbook and console UI with per-tenant headroom view
PRs: unit + integration tests and code review
comments: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting — alignment on SLA tiers and headroom definition. Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Jenna (SRE), Victor (Product). Action: Aisha to produce metric spec.
2025-02-18: Metric spec v1 posted to Confluence. Included RPS, token/sec, queue depth, and kernel-use fraction. Product asked to add 'burst allowance' per contract.

2025-02-21: Simulation run #1 (100 tenants, one gold burst) — controller prevented pool eviction but introduced 18% extra cost. Trade-off discussed: allow slightly larger step for gold tenants with budget cap.

2025-02-25: Design review with runtime team. Marco proposed a conservative default step of 20% upscale, 15% downscale, with an override for gold up to 40% when projected SLA violation probability >0.7. Runtime raised concern about KV cache cold-start; we added a 'kv-warm' flag to postpone strict downscale for 10 minutes post-upscale.
2025-03-01: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1123 - controller skeleton and tests. Requesting review from @sre-team and @runtime-core.

2025-03-02: Simulation run #7 (heterogeneous bursts): gold tenants maintained 95p latency within 1.15x baseline; median cost delta +9% vs baseline but system avoided 3 tenant-facing incidents. SRE recommends canary.
2025-03-02: Blocking note: need routing tag propagation (ENG-21042) before canary; added as dependency.
notes: Design decisions: overlay controller to reduce blast radius; orchestrator retains final authority — simpler rollback and audit trail.
Trade-offs: tighter per-tenant guarantees increase overall unit cost; we expose a per-tenant SLA flag so customers can opt-in.
Safety knobs: max_step, min_replicas_per_pool, negative_scale_soft_floor, cooldown_seconds, kv_warm_delay_seconds, rollback_latency_threshold.
Testing plan: unit tests for synthesizer math, integration tests with orchestrator accept/reject, long-run sim to detect oscillation modes.
Operational: add Grafana dashboard with proposed vs accepted deltas, per-tenant headroom, and cooldown heatmap. Prepare runbook for manual override.
Next: finalize API schema for controller->orchestrator (proposal: /v1/pool_delta with reason-coded deltas).
